1.explanation: FilterableMultiSelect.js is where the ‘id’ prop is passed directly onto the <input> and the wrapper (<ListBox.Field>), so two instances with the same id produce duplicate id attributes in the DOM. That file also renders <ListBox.Menu role=“group”>, overriding its default listbox role, which leads to ‘option’ roles not being nested in a listbox container. Both of these problems must be fixed in FilterableMultiSelect.js.
1.bug_scenario: When two <MultiSelect.Filterable> components are rendered with the same “id” prop (in this reproduction, “carbon-multiselect-example”), the rendered <input> and the menu container both receive that same id, causing duplicate-id accessibility violations. In addition, FilterableMultiSelect overrides the ListBox.Menu’s default role="listbox" with role="group", so the inner <div> elements carrying role="option" aren’t actually contained in a valid listbox, triggering WAI-ARIA role errors.
